title: dot: a node of a cluster in a rank=max set panics build_skeleton (cluster.rs:328) where C reads a NULL rank leader
dot: with splines=ortho and concentrate=true, the port drops an edge that C routes and draws
body:
With `concentrate=true`, a back edge that runs opposite a forward edge between the same two nodes is marked `IGNORED` (its opposite gets `conc_opp_flag`). `orthoEdges` keeps only one edge per node pair, the first in `agfstnode`/`agfstout` order, which here is the `IGNORED` edge `13 -> 14`, and gives it the spline. C's SVG emitter draws any edge that has `ED_spl`, so `13 -> 14` appears, while `14 -> 13` has no spline and does not. The port routes the same edge, but its layout-to-render export drops the splines of `IGNORED` edges, so neither edge is drawn. `-Tdot` agrees in both programs (neither writes a `pos` for these edges). Only the drawn output differs.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph G {
splines="ortho";
concentrate="true";
"8" -> "9";
"8" -> "13";
"9" -> "14";
"14" -> "13";
"13" -> "14";
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv                               # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.svg
+++ rust.svg
-<!-- 13->14 -->
-<g id="edge5" class="edge">
-<title>13->14</title>
-<path fill="none" stroke="black" d="M40.5,-33.98C40.5,-33.98 40.5,-62.55 40.5,-62.55"/>
-<polygon fill="black" stroke="black" points="37,-62.55 40.5,-72.55 44,-62.55 37,-62.55"/>
-</g>
```

**Root cause**

C: `class2` marks the edge `IGNORED` (`lib/dotgen/class2.c:266-271`). `orthoEdges` skips the second edge of each node pair under `Concentrate` (`lib/ortho/ortho.c:1216-1232`) and assigns splines to the kept edge whatever its type. `attach_attrs_and_arrows` skips `IGNORED` edges when it writes `pos` (`lib/common/output.c:350-353`), but `emit_edge_graphics` draws from `ED_spl` with no type check (`lib/common/emit.c:2366`).

Port: `Output::collect` keeps a spline only if `edge_type != IGNORED` (`crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/dotgen/output.rs:81-96`). That filter is right for the `pos` attribute but also removes the edge from the renderer, so the SVG loses `13 -> 14`.

Suggested fix: export the spline of an `IGNORED` edge to the renderer but keep it out of `pos`/`lp` in the `-Tdot`/`-Txdot`/`-Tjson` writers, as C's `attach_attrs` does. The full case also lacks C's `Orthogonal edges do not currently handle edge labels` warning (stderr only).

dot pack: with one component, C lays out the root while the _cc_0 subgraph exists, which applies the root rank and cloned clusters a second time
body:
With `pack` or `packmode` set and only one connected component (or a non-default `ratio`), C still runs `cccomps` first, which creates a `_cc_0` subgraph of the root (holding clones of the top-level clusters), and only then lays out the root with `dotLayout(g)`. The `_cc_0` subgraph is deleted after the layout. While the root is laid out, rank and cluster processing see `_cc_0` like any other subgraph. It inherits the root's `rank` attribute as its default, so a root-level `rank=max|min|same` puts every node of the component on one rank. Its cloned clusters are seen a second time ("n was already in a rankset, deleted from cluster", "removing empty cluster", and newrank cluster ranks). The port lays out the plain root in this case. Its output equals C's output *without* `pack` for all four cases. In `s33006` this changes the exit status: C ranks everything into one rank, while the port fails with `trouble in init_rank` and exits 1.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph G {
pack=true;
rank=max;
a -> b;
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv                              # port
```

**Root cause**

C: `doDot` (`lib/dotgen/dotinit.c:465-472`) calls `cccomps(g, &ncc, 0)`, and when `ncc == 1` (or with a ratio, `dotinit.c:494`) it calls `dotLayout(g)` on the root. The components are only deleted afterwards (`dotinit.c:502-503`). `cccomps` (`lib/pack/ccomps.c:470-474`) creates `_cc_<i>` with `agsubg(g, ...)`, so its attributes are the root's defaults, and `subGInduce`/`projectG` (`ccomps.c:378-422`) clone the root's subgraphs and clusters inside it (with `agcopyattr`). `dot1_rank` then runs `collapse_sets(g, g)` (`lib/dotgen/rank.c:354-371`). `rank_set_class` (`rank.c:225`) reads `_cc_0`'s inherited `rank` and collapses the whole component. Under newrank, `dot2_rank` walks the cloned clusters as well.

Port: `do_dot` (`crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/dotgen/pack.rs:408-410`) returns `d.dot_layout()` on the unmodified root graph when `ccs.len() == 1` (or with a ratio), so no `_cc_0` subgraph exists during ranking.

Suggested fix: in that branch, lay out the root with the component subgraph present: add a `_cc_0` subgraph whose attributes are the root's graph defaults, containing all nodes, with the projected subgraph and cluster clones from `cccomps`. Then drop it before output. `cccomps.rs` already computes the projection (`CComp::subgraphs`).

title: dot: the renderer rebuilds ND_lw/ND_rw/ND_ht from width/height, so `style=diagonals` and abandoned layouts draw nodes the wrong size
body:
C draws nodes from the layout's `ND_lw`, `ND_rw` and `ND_ht`. The port's render model sets `lw = rw = width/2` and `ht = height*72`, which loses two things: the extra `ND_rw` that dot gives a node with self-loops (kept when `splines=""`/`none` or `curved` skips or undoes `resetRW`), and the swapped dimensions of a flipped `rankdir` when the layout is abandoned. `style=diagonals` on an ellipse (`Mcircle_hack`, which uses `ND_rw` alone) draws its two chords about 6pt shorter on each side. After an abandoned `rankdir=RL` layout (`install_in_rank` error, seed 21064), C draws the ellipses `rx=18 ry=27` and the port draws `rx=27 ry=18`.

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph "G" {
splines="";
"n7" [style="diagonals"];
"n7" -- "n7":"ne" [];
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv                               # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.svg
+++ rust.svg
-<polyline fill="none" stroke="black" points="56.76,-31.5 -2.76,-31.5"/>
-<polyline fill="none" stroke="black" points="56.76,-4.5 -2.76,-4.5"/>
+<polyline fill="none" stroke="black" points="50.81,-31.5 3.19,-31.5"/>
+<polyline fill="none" stroke="black" points="50.81,-4.5 3.19,-4.5"/>
```

**Root cause**

C, self-loop space: `dot_position` adds the loop width to `ND_rw` (`lib/dotgen/position.c:244`, `:260`), and `dot_splines_` swaps it back with `resetRW` only for curved and ortho (`lib/dotgen/dotsplines.c:187-193`, `:239-252`; it returns early for `EDGETYPE_NONE` at `:239`). `poly_gencode` scales by `xsize = (ND_lw+ND_rw)/INCH2PS(ND_width)` and `ysize = ND_ht/INCH2PS(ND_height)` (`lib/common/shapes.c:2950-2951`), and `Mcircle_hack` (`lib/common/shapes.c:547-564`) uses `p.x = ND_rw(n) * .6614`. With `lw=27, rw=45` C draws the chords from x+29.76 to x-29.76. The port's `RNode` is built with `lw: w/2, rw: w/2, ht: height*72` (`crates/graphviz-pure-render/src/emit/model.rs:298-308`), so `mcircle_hack` (`crates/graphviz-pure-render/src/emit/shapes.rs:341-351`) gets `rw=36`. Only `lw+rw` crosses over from the layout, through the `width` written by `Output::collect`/`apply` (`crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/dotgen/output.rs:56-62`, `:178-182`).

C, abandoned layout (seed 21064, `rankdir=RL` and an `install_in_rank` failure): no postprocessing runs, so `ND_lw+ND_rw` and `ND_ht` keep the rotated values (36 and 54) while `ND_width`/`ND_height` are 54/36. `xsize`/`ysize` then give `rx=18, ry=27`. The port again rebuilds from width/height and draws `rx=27, ry=18`.

Suggested fix: carry the layout's `lw`, `rw` and `ht` per node into the render model (for example as hidden attributes next to `width`), and use them in `poly_gencode`'s `xsize`/`ysize` and in `mcircle_hack`, instead of rebuilding them from `width`/`height`.

**Cases**

3 fuzz case(s): seeds 31148, 32581, 21064. Seeds 31148 (`splines=curved`) and 32581 (`splines=""`) are the diagonals case. Seed 21064 is the abandoned `rankdir=RL` layout (its minimised form: `rankdir=RL`, a cluster with a self-loop node, `rank=source`). It also lacks C's `was already in a rankset` warning (stderr only).
Regenerate a case with `python3 -I scripts/fuzz-gen.py --seed N` (checked byte for byte for seed 31148).

title: dot pack: clusters are drawn in subgraph order, so the duplicated and reordered GD_clust entries of copyClusterInfo are lost
body:
With `pack`/`packmode`, C rebuilds the root's cluster list (`GD_clust`) from the components, in component order, and draws exactly that list. The port's renderer rebuilds the cluster tree from the subgraph tree instead. When a node belongs to two non-nested top-level clusters, C's list holds the same cluster twice and draws it twice (two identical `<g class="cluster">` groups). When the components' clusters are not in subgraph order, C draws them in component order (`cluster_0, cluster_5, cluster_3` below) and the port in declaration order. The geometry is the same; only the number and order of the cluster groups differ.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph G {
pack=8;
subgraph cluster_0 { a }
subgraph cluster_1 { a }
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv                              # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.svg
+++ rust.svg
@@ -14,6 +14,2 @@
 </g>
-<g id="clust1" class="cluster">
-<title>cluster_0</title>
-<polygon fill="none" stroke="black" points="136,-120 136,-172 206,-172 206,-120 136,-120"/>
-</g>
 <!-- a -->
```

Second reproducer, for the order (`r4/diff/s35883.gv` minimised):

```dot
graph G {
packmode="node";
subgraph cluster_0 { a }
subgraph cluster_3 { b }
subgraph cluster_5 { c }
x -- a;
x -- c;
}
```

C draws `cluster_0, cluster_5, cluster_3`, and the port draws `cluster_0, cluster_3, cluster_5` (the boxes are identical).

**Root cause**

C: `cccomps` (`lib/pack/ccomps.c:437`) makes one component per derived node. `deriveClusters` (`lib/pack/ccomps.c:262`) maps a node of two clusters to the last one only (and prints the "belongs to two non-nested clusters" error), but `unionNodes` (`lib/pack/ccomps.c:330`) still adds every node of *each* cluster to that cluster's component, and `subGInduce` projects both clusters into both components. Each component's layout keeps the first cluster, so `copyClusterInfo` (`lib/dotgen/dotinit.c:412`) appends it to `GD_clust(root)` once per component. `copyClusterInfo` also orders the root list by component, then by the order of each component's `GD_clust`. `emit_clusters` (`lib/common/emit.c:3790`) walks `GD_clust(g)` as it is, duplicates included.

Port: `copy_cluster_info` builds the same list in `d.graphs[0].clust` (`crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/dotgen/pack.rs:470-478`). But `Output::collect` only records each cluster's box by subgraph index (`crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/dotgen/output.rs:65-75`), and the renderer derives `root_clusters` from the subgraph tree in declaration order (`crates/graphviz-pure-render/src/emit/model.rs:455`), so multiplicity and order are lost.

Suggested fix: export the layout's `GD_clust` order (with repeats) per graph, for example as an ordered child list on each subgraph, and have `model.rs` use it when present instead of the subgraph tree.

5 fuzz case(s), seeds 1062, 1548, 28, 11551, 35883. Regenerate one with `python3 -I scripts/fuzz-gen.py --seed N` (checked byte for byte for seed 1062); run it with `-Kdot -Tsvg`.

title: neato splines=polyline: route to a compass port on the node boundary ends 0.1pt off from C's for some node widths
body:
For an edge routed with `splines=polyline` (or `spline`) to a compass port on the head node's boundary (`"10":n`), the port and C produce different polylines for some node widths, even with identical node positions. In C the path from the tail is slightly bent (x drifts from 29.241 to 29.265) and in the port it is perfectly vertical; with other widths the head end point itself differs by 0.1pt in x (C at the node centre, the port 0.1pt right of it, or the reverse). `splines=line` agrees. The node positions agree exactly, so the difference is in routing.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph "fuzz 12614" {
layout=neato;
splines="polyline";
mode="hier";
"10" [label="Start"];
"9" -> "10":"n" [xlabel="\T", color="white"];
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv                             # port
```

```diff
+++ port

+<text xml:space="preserve" text-anchor="middle" x="25.78" y="-47.04" font-family="Times,serif" font-size="14.00">9</text>
 </g>
```

**Root cause**

Root cause not yet confirmed. Narrowed down with `-n` (fixed positions): two nodes stacked vertically, `9 -> 10:n`, `splines=polyline`, head node `width=0.81` differs, while `width=0.75, 0.8, 0.82, 0.83, 0.85, 0.9, 1.0` agree (at 0.83 C itself ends 0.1pt off-centre and the port agrees). So it is a near-degenerate case in the shortest-path / visibility routing of a point on the obstacle boundary: C `lib/neatogen/neatosplines.c:501-516` (`getPath` → `Pobspath`, `lib/pathplan/cvt.c`) and `makePolyline` (`neatosplines.c:519-527`); port `crates/graphviz-pure-geom/src/pathplan/cvt.rs` and `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/routing.rs` (`make_obstacle`, line 52). A likely candidate is a different floating-point result in the obstacle polygon vertices (`makeObstacle`, `neatosplines.c` ellipse branch) or in the in-polygon / visibility tests, but this was not verified. ```
C: `pos="e,29.16,36.482 29.126,71.526 ..."`, port: `pos="e,29.26,36.483 29.026,71.859 ..."`.

title: parser: unquoted keywords (node, edge, graph, ...) are accepted as attribute names, values and ports; C reports a syntax error
body:
The port accepts the DOT keywords `node`, `edge`, `graph`, `digraph`, `subgraph` and `strict`, unquoted, as an attribute name, an attribute value or a port name. C rejects them with a syntax error and exits 1. In the port, `packmode=node;`, `a [label=edge]`, `a [node=1]` and `a:graph -> b` all parse and render with exit status 0. In C, each one gives `syntax error in line N near '<keyword>'`.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph G {
packmode=node;
a [label=edge];
a:graph -> b;
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv                              # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.stderr
+++ rust.stderr
-Error: repro.gv: syntax error in line 2 near 'node'
-exit 1
+exit 0
```

C writes no SVG. The port writes a full drawing (`rust.svg`).

**Root cause**

C, `lib/cgraph/grammar.y:209` (`attrassignment : atom '=' atom`), `:181-183` (`node : atom | atom ':' atom | atom ':' atom ':' atom`) and `:225-226` (`atom : T_atom | qatom`). The scanner returns `T_node`, `T_edge`, `T_graph`, `T_digraph`, `T_subgraph` and `T_strict` for the keywords (`grammar.y:131`), and none of them is an `atom`, so yacc reports a syntax error.

Port, `crates/graphviz-pure-parser/src/parser.rs:225-243` (`parse_value_or_port_atom`): if the next token is a keyword, it is taken as an atom with the keyword's text. This is called for graph attribute values (`parser.rs:380`), attribute-list keys and values (`parser.rs:465`, `:467`) and port and compass names (`parser.rs:586`, `:589`).

Suggested fix: `parse_value_or_port_atom` should accept only atom tokens, the same as `parse_atom`, so that a keyword in these places gives the port's syntax error. Quoted keywords (`"node"`) are `T_qatom` in C and remain valid.

**Cases**

No fuzz case. The generator always quotes values. Found by hand while triaging the dot pack cases (`packmode=node;`).

title: stderr: C warnings the port does not print (unknown port, HTML attributes, unplaced labels, rankset/cluster, ortho labels, touching nodes, multispline failures, printpath dump)
body:
C prints several `agwarningf` warnings (and one `agerrorf` follow-up dump) that the port leaves out. The output and exit status are the same; only stderr differs. Each warning is a small change on its own, and they are grouped here as one checklist. **Reproducer** ```dot graph G { splines=none a [xlabel=q, label=<
x
>] a:nosuch -- b [label=x] } ``` ```sh GVBINDIR= dot -Tsvg repro.gv graphviz-pure -Tsvg repro.gv ``` **C output vs port** ```diff --- c.stderr +++ rust.stderr -Warning: Illegal attribute FOO in - ignored -in label of node a -Warning: node a, port nosuch unrecognized -Warning: no position for edge with label x ``` **Root cause** (checklist) - [ ] **Unknown port name**: `unrecognized()` (`lib/common/shapes.c:362-365`), called from `poly_port` (`shapes.c:2909-2910`) and `record_port` (`shapes.c:3751-3752`) when `compassPort` returns true. Also covers `record_port`'s `unrecognized compass point '%s' - ignored` (`shapes.c:3748-3749`). In the port, `compass_port` returns that flag (`crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/common/ports.rs:126`), but the callers at `ports.rs:385` and `ports.rs:407` ignore it. C warns once per port resolution, so the number of repeats should follow C's call sites. - [ ] **HTML attribute warnings**: `doAttrs` (`lib/common/htmllex.c:540-552`) warns `Illegal attribute %s in %s - ignored` and sets `warn`, and `make_label` then adds `in label of `. The port's HTML parser (`crates/graphviz-pure-geom/src/html_label.rs`, see `parse_html_report` at line 1417 and the `in label of` handling at line 2105) reports only fatal HTML errors. title: stderr: DOT syntax error message wording and line differ from C
body:
The port's DOT syntax error message is worded differently from C's, and for some errors it reports a different line. Both exit with status 1 and write no output for the failing graph (graphs before the error are still rendered, as in C), so only stderr differs.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph G {
 a -> b
 c [label="abc

]
 d
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Tsvg repro.gv
graphviz-pure -Tsvg repro.gv
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.stderr
+++ rust.stderr
-Error: repro.gv: syntax error in line 7 scanning a quoted string (missing endquote? longer than 16384?)
-String starting:"abc
-
-]
- d
-
+Error: repro.gv: DOT syntax error at line 3, column 11: unclosed quoted string literal
```

A plain token error (`repro2.gv`: `c -> ;`):

```diff
-Error: repro2.gv: syntax error in line 3 near ';'
+Error: repro2.gv: DOT syntax error at line 3, column 7: expected identifier or string literal, found Semi
```

**Root cause**

C's message comes from `aagerror` (`lib/cgraph/scan.l:150-185`): `"<file>: syntax error in line N"`, followed by `near '<yytext>'`. When yytext is empty it instead reports the lexer state (`scanning a quoted string ... String starting:"...`, `scanning a HTML string ...`, `scanning a /*...*/ comment ...`). The line is the scanner's current `line_num`, which is where bison detects the error. For an unclosed string that is end of file. The port formats `GraphvizError::SyntaxError` as `DOT syntax error at line {line}, column {col}: {message}` (`crates/graphviz-pure-core/src/error.rs:6`, printed by `crates/graphviz-pure-cli/src/main.rs:241,272`). The unclosed-string error is raised at the opening quote (`crates/graphviz-pure-parser/src/lexer.rs:416`). Suggested fix: keep the parser, but format errors as C does (`syntax error in line N near 'TOKEN'`, using the token's source text, with C's lexer-state suffixes) and report the line at which C's lookahead token ends (end of file for an unterminated string, HTML string or comment).

**Cases**

title: neato mode=KK model=circuit: C indexes the conductance matrix by AGSEQ (1-based) and crashes
body:
With `mode=KK` and `model=circuit`, C Graphviz 16.1.0 crashes even on a connected triangle. `circuit_model` fills the `nG x nG` conductance matrix with `Gm[i][j]` where `i`, `j` are `AGSEQ` of the edge's endpoints. Node sequence numbers start at 1 (and on a packed component they are root-graph numbers), so the last node writes through `Gm[nG]`, a pointer read past the row-pointer array. C dies with SIGSEGV/SIGBUS, or, when the stray pointer happens to be writable (as in fuzz case 33861, which crashes only in some runs), lays out from a corrupted matrix. The port indexes by the node's layout id (`ND_id`), as every other neato distance model does, and produces a drawing.

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph G {
layout=neato;
mode="KK";
model="circuit";
a -- b;
b -- c;
c -- a;
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv                             # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
C:    exit status 139 (SIGSEGV), no output (every run on the 3-node reproducer;
      2-4 of 10 runs on the fuzz case s33861, the other runs print an SVG)
port: exit status 0, SVG of the triangle
```

**Root cause**

C: `lib/neatogen/circuit.c:44-50` uses `AGSEQ(agtail(e))`/`AGSEQ(aghead(e))` as matrix indices; `AGSEQ` comes from `agnextseq` (`lib/cgraph/graph.c:156-159`, pre-increment, so the first node is 1). `new_array` (`lib/neatogen/stuff.c:39-51`) allocates exactly `nG` row pointers. Called from `kkNeato` (`lib/neatogen/neatoinit.c:1245-1256`). Crash reports for the fuzz case show `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` in `circuit_model < neatoLayout < neato_layout`. (The stress-majorization path, `model=circuit` without `mode=KK`, uses `lib/neatogen/stress.c`'s own `circuit_model` on the vertex array and does not crash.)

Port: `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/stuff.rs:445-458` (`circuit_model_kk`) indexes by `g.nodes[..].id`, the 0-based node index within the component.

The port should not reproduce a wild write. Recommend wontfix (upstream bug: use `ND_id` as `shortest_path` and `subset_model` do).

title: neato mode=ipsep with a node in two clusters: C underflows ntoplevel and aborts on a SIZE_MAX allocation; the port draws the graph
body:
With `mode=ipsep`, neato builds a cluster map that counts the nodes outside every top-level cluster as `agnnodes(g)` minus one per (cluster, member) pair. A node that belongs to two non-nested clusters is subtracted twice, so the unsigned count wraps to `SIZE_MAX`, and `gv_calloc(SIZE_MAX, 8)` makes C exit with status 1 and no output. The port computes the top-level node list directly (nodes not assigned to any cluster), so it never wraps, and it renders the graph with exit status 0.

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph "G" {
layout=neato;
mode="ipsep";
subgraph "cluster_0" {
"n1" -- "n4";
}
subgraph "cluster_1" {
"n1" [];
}
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv                             # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
C stderr:
-integer overflow when trying to allocate 18446744073709551615 * 8 bytes
-[exit status 1]   (no stdout)
port:
+[exit status 0]   (a complete SVG with both clusters)
```

**Root cause**

C: `lib/neatogen/neatoinit.c:206` starts `cdata.ntoplevel = agnnodes_z(g)`, `neatoinit.c:231` decrements it once per cluster member (duplicates included), `neatoinit.c:236` allocates `gv_calloc(cdata.ntoplevel, sizeof(size_t))`; the overflow check in `gv_calloc` prints the message and exits.

Port: `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/cola.rs:21-47` (`cluster_map`) builds `toplevel` with a filter over an `assigned` bitmap, so a doubly assigned node is simply not top level.

The port could match C by emitting the same message and exiting 1 when the C count would wrap, but that would mean copying an upstream overflow bug. Recommend wontfix; mention it in the C bugs ledger.

title: fdp (C): cluster layouts depend on heap addresses and vary run to run
neato-family multispline router: ties in the triangle shortest path are broken by GTS's pointer-hash face order
body:
Edges with multi-edges or boundary ports (`splines=true|spline|polyline`) go through `makeMultiSpline`, which runs Dijkstra (`triPath`) over the triangles of a constrained Delaunay triangulation. When two triangle paths have exactly the same cost — typically a symmetric layout where the edge can go above or below a node — the winner depends on the face numbering. C numbers the faces in the order `gts_surface_foreach_face` visits them, which is GTS's `GHashTable` order of face *pointers*; the port numbers them in creation order. The port then mirrors the route (here below the head node instead of above it).

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph "G" {
layout=sfdp;
splines="true";
edge [headport="e"];
"n5" [shape="circle", label="→ arrow"];
{"n5"} -- "n12";
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Ksfdp -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Ksfdp -Tsvg repro.gv                              # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.svg
+++ rust.svg
@@ -26 +26 @@
-<path fill="none" stroke="black" d="M85.73,-34.99C137.89,-25.98 228.99,-13.78 306.94,-21.46 317.19,-22.47 321.8,-20.68 329.21,-27.83 334.35,-32.79 334.19,-43.11 334.19,-43.11"/>
+<path fill="none" stroke="black" d="M85.73,-51.44C137.89,-60.45 228.99,-72.65 306.94,-64.97 317.19,-63.96 321.8,-65.75 329.21,-58.6 334.35,-53.64 334.19,-43.31 334.19,-43.31"/>
```

**Root cause**

C, `lib/neatogen/delaunay.c:447-480` (`mkSurface`): face indices come from `gts_surface_foreach_face(s, cntFace, ...)`, i.e. GTS's hash-table iteration over face pointers; `lib/neatogen/multispline.c:1104-1148` (`triPath`) keeps the first-found parent on equal distances (`N_VAL(pq, adjn) < d`).

Port, `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/multispline.rs:263-335` (`mk_surface`): faces are numbered in creation order (a documented deviation, `docs/porting/neato.md`, "The `makeMultiSpline` router's triangulation numbers faces in creation order, not GTS's pointer-hash order").

Confirmed by experiment: dumping C's face order with a `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` shim around `gts_surface_foreach_face` and feeding it to a patched port that renumbers its (identical) triangles in that order makes the port match C byte for byte on all three cases. The order is address-dependent in C: an intermediate minimisation of s33154 gives two different C outputs from run to run, and both are reproduced by the port when given that run's face order.

Why the port does not match: C's result depends on heap addresses of GTS faces, which the port cannot reproduce in general (it would mean modelling GLib's direct-hash bucket order over malloc addresses). The port keeps the deterministic creation order. Suggest closing as wontfix (upstream nondeterminism); revisit only if a cheap model of the hash order turns out to match C for the usual allocation pattern.

body:
With `start=random` and no number after it (neato, fdp, sfdp), or fdp with `start=regular` or `start=self`, C seeds its random number generator from the clock, `time(NULL)`. The same input therefore gives a different layout in C every second. The port uses a fixed seed instead (1, the value C uses when no `start` is given), so its output is deterministic. It can match C only by chance, so these cases are not port bugs. title: Linux/WASM: portable libm differs from Apple's pow/sin/cos/atan2 (2470/2589 e2e)
body:
On Linux and in the WASM build, the port uses portable math functions (`graphviz_pure_core::math::portable`), because macOS's `libsystem_m`, the libm that C Graphviz uses on macOS and that the goldens were made with, is closed source. Apple's `pow`, `sin`, `cos` and `atan2` give a different last bit from both the musl-derived `libm` crate and correctly rounded implementations on some inputs. One bit is enough to move a force-directed layout. With Apple's libm the port matches C on all 2,589 `gv-diff e2e` outputs. With portable math it matches 2,470: 114 sfdp, 3 fdp, 1 circo and 1 main (`gallery_beautify_1_1cfb90`, an sfdp graph). The same files explain the portable layout ratchets: main 564/565, sfdp 183/297, fdp 382/386, circo 279/280. twopi's one extra portable miss, `wild_gv16_graphs_arrows_148b6b`, is one of the C-unstable arrows graphs. Linux aarch64, Linux x86_64 and wasm32 produce bit-identical output to each other (`docs/porting/libm.md`, "Linux and wasm32").

**Reproducer**

The smallest affected file is `tests/wild/gallery_beautify_1_1cfb90.gv` (the main corpus's only portable miss):

```dot
digraph G {
```

**Root cause**

All transcendental calls go through `crates/graphviz-pure-core/src/math/mod.rs` (`PORTABLE` at line 25). **Why the port does not match:** matching bit for bit would mean reproducing Apple's closed `pow`/`sin`/`cos`/`atan2` from the binary (the published Libm `Source/ARM/*.s` files are empty). That raises a licensing question and has not been done. Correctly rounded `sin`/`cos` would be worse (circo 274/280), and correctly rounded `atan2` gains nothing. The port is exact on macOS and deterministic across all other platforms. The portable baselines (`*.portable.json`) catch regressions there.

title: twopi: edge routes on the arrows graphs change from run to run in C (floating-point tie)
body:
On the `arrows` family of graphs (`twopi`, `splines=true`), C Graphviz 16.1.0 does not give the same output from one run to the next. Nodes `Z`, `i` and `I` (and their mirror images lower down) are exactly vertically aligned, so the edge between `Z` and `I` has a tie: it can run straight, pass the obstacle in between on the left, or pass it on the right. The same C binary gives 3 or 4 different SVGs over 20 runs of each of the 8 files. The port is deterministic. It always produces one of these routes, but its combination of routes for the whole file matches a C run only some of the time (in 20 runs, `oldarrows` matched 2 of them and the other 7 files matched none). This is why `gv-diff` shows twopi at 282/289 exact and why `gv-diff e2e` records the 8 files as unstable and skips them (`tests/golden/e2e.json`, `unstable`).

In the port this is `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/neatosplines.rs:135` (`spline_edges_route`) and `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/routing.rs:193` (`make_spline`). The node positions are the same in every C run; only the edge routes change. The C output still varies with `MallocPreScribble=1 MallocScribble=1`, so reads of uninitialised heap memory are unlikely, and the variation probably comes from something that depends on addresses. The exact C statement has **not been confirmed yet**. One candidate is `cmpitems` (`lib/neatogen/neatosplines.c:124`), which orders multi-edge keys by node pointer, but no link from it to the route has been shown. The documentation used to say this tie differs from build to build (`docs/porting/circo-twopi.md:32-37`). In fact the same build differs from run to run.

**Why the port does not match:** no single deterministic output can match an output that changes between runs. The port computes the routes in a fixed order and returns the same SVG every time. We propose closing this as upstream C nondeterminism. If the C source is found and turns out to be deterministic under some condition, the port could follow it.

title: -Tplain: C prints freed memory for Latin-1/entity-converted labels (use-after-free in canon)
body:
With `-Tplain` and `-Tplain-ext`, C prints freed memory in place of a node label when the label text changed during conversion (`latin1ToUTF8` for `charset=latin1`, or `htmlEntityUTF8` for entities such as `∞`) and does not need quoting. The label field then contains whatever the freed allocation holds: on macOS a control byte that differs between runs (`^E`, `^F`, ...). The port prints the converted label (`été`).

**Reproducer** (the file is Latin-1: the label bytes are `E9 74 E9`)

```dot
graph G {
charset=latin1
a [label="\xe9t\xe9"]
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Tplain repro.gv     # two different outputs over 6 runs
graphviz-pure -Tplain repro.gv
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.plain
+++ rust.plain
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 graph 1 0.75 0.5
-node a 0.375 0.25 0.75 0.5 \x05 solid ellipse black lightgrey
+node a 0.375 0.25 0.75 0.5 été solid ellipse black lightgrey
 stop
```

**Root cause**

`canon` (`lib/common/output.c:103-108`) interns the label with `agstrdup` and passes it to `agstrcanon`, then frees it with `agstrfree`. When the string needs no quotes, `_agstrcanon` returns its argument itself (`lib/cgraph/write.c:202`, `return arg;`) instead of the scratch buffer. If nothing else holds a reference to the interned string (the converted text is new), `agstrfree` releases it and `writenodeandport`/`write_plain` (`lib/common/output.c:153-158`, and line 202 for edge labels) print a dangling pointer. This is a use-after-free in C. The port (`crates/graphviz-pure-render/src/emit/output.rs:219-221`, `canon_str`) prints the converted text, which is what C intends.

**Why the port should not match:** the C output is undefined behaviour and changes between runs. `gv-diff render` skips these references (`crates/graphviz-pure-diff/src/render.rs:21-46`, `UNSTABLE`). This should be reported upstream: `canon` should copy the result before `agstrfree`.

**Cases**

10 render-corpus references per format (`plain` and `plain-ext`): `charset_Latin1`, `charset_b34`, `charset_b56`, `charset_b60`, `charset_latin1_html`, `charset_latin1_mixed`, `gallery__index_7_fe2a40`, `gv16_graphs_Symbol_af1a2d`, `gv16_graphs_b34_ca01c7`, `gv16_graphs_b56_36f937`.

title: -Txdot: C prints its own string constants for HTML cells with STYLE="dashed" (out-of-bounds read in xdot_style)
body:
With `-Txdot` (and the other formats built on the xdot renderer: `-Tdot` output's `_ldraw_` attributes, `-Tjson`), an HTML-like table cell with `STYLE="dashed"` or `STYLE="dotted"` makes C print a run of unrelated string constants from its own binary into the drawing: format strings, file names and assertion texts. The port prints the style the cell asked for (`S 6 -dashed`). **Reproducer** ```dot digraph { n [shape=box label=<
x
>] } ``` ```sh GVBINDIR= dot -Txdot repro.gv graphviz-pure -Txdot repro.gv ``` **C output vs port** (C's line shortened) ```diff -_ldraw_="S 5 -solid c 7 -#000000 p 4 17.5 4 17.5 32.8 36.5 32.8 36.5 4 S 1095 -dashed(dotted,invis,invisible,bold,setlinewidth,filled,unfilled,tapered,gvrender_set_style: unsupported style %s - ignoring\n,gvrender_usershape,gvrender.c,name,name[0],color %s,%s is not a known color. ... +_ldraw_="S 5 -solid c 7 -#000000 p 4 17.5 4 17.5 32.8 36.5 32.8 36.5 4 S 6 -dashed c 7 -#000000 p 4 20.5 7 20.5 29.8 33.5 29.8 33.5 7 F 14 11 -Times-Roman c 7 -#000000 T 23.5 12.8 -1 7 1 -x ", ``` **Root cause** `doBorder` (`lib/common/htmltable.c:261-268`) passes the style as `sptr[0] = "dashed"`, a plain string literal. Style lists elsewhere come from `parse_style`, where each entry is `name\0arg\0arg\0\0`: a name followed by its arguments and an empty string. `xdot_style` (`plugin/core/gvrender_core_dot.c:186-199`) relies on that layout: after the name it skips one NUL and, while the next byte is not NUL, reads arguments. For the literal `"dashed"` the next bytes belong to whatever constants the compiler placed after it, so C reads past the end of the string (undefined behaviour) until it happens to hit two NULs in a row. What it prints depends on the binary's string-table layout. The port builds the same style in `crates/graphviz-pure-render/src/emit/html.rs:181` and prints just the name, which is what C means to do. **Why the port should not match:** the C output is an out-of-bounds read; its content depends on the compiler and linker, not on the graph. `gv-diff render` does not include this case. It should be reported upstream: `doBorder` should pass a properly terminated style (e.g. `"dashed\0\0"`) or `xdot_style` should not assume arguments follow. **Cases** Not a fuzz case: found while porting the renderer (`docs/porting/render.md`, Known differences). The fuzz generator does not produce HTML-like labels. **Files** `tests/fuzz-open/034-html-cell-dashed-style-overread` Visual diff: {{SITE}}/whats-left/html-cell-dashed-style-overread/
